findings.title: Player-pawn stand-down blocks vanilla in a mental break even when the driver will never cast for that pawn
findings.detail: OthersStandDown returns HasWorker for every player pawn. With BreakCasting off (the default), ControlOf returns Control.None for a pawn in a mental state (AbilityAI.cs:568), so the driver never casts for it. Vanilla is still told no, so a berserk colonist's aiCanUse fallback ability (the host pattern the file header describes) is cast by nobody. This is not what happens without this mod. With BreakCasting on, the same is true for abilities no hook claims while Unclaimed is off. One change: in the player branch, return Handles(pawn, ability) instead of HasWorker when pawn.InMentalState, so vanilla keeps its break behaviour unless this mod actually takes the pawn over.

findings.title: Right-click on one pawn's ungrouped ability gizmo sets the mode for every selected pawn
findings.detail: parms.multipleSelected is true exactly when several pawns' Command_Ability gizmos for the same def are drawn as separate buttons (ShowPawnDetailsWith); vanilla only merges them into one button when def.groupAbility is set (GroupsWith). OpenMenu (AbilityAIAutocast.cs:144-145) still collects every selected pawn with the ability, so right-clicking the button labelled 'Ability (B)' changes A and C too, while the '(current)' marker and the badge show only B's mode. Change OpenMenu to gather the other selected pawns only when clicked.def.groupAbility is true. Then the title rule at :196 is backwards: when multipleSelected is true the per-pawn LabelCap is accurate and the def label is not.

evidence.ref: Verse/GizmoGridDrawer.cs:279-290 (multipleSelected from ShowPawnDetailsWith); RimWorld/Command_Ability.cs:144 (GroupsWith requires def.groupAbility); Source/AbilityAI/AbilityAIAutocast.cs:144

findings.title: Doc comment on the stand-down patch says vanilla keeps unclaimed abilities, which no longer holds for player pawns
findings.detail: The comment at AbilityAIMod.cs:80 lists 'an unclaimed ability with Unclaimed off' as a case where vanilla keeps its own behaviour. Since the player branch was added to OthersStandDown, that holds only for non-player pawns. Player pawns in a lord (AbilityAI.cs:571, Control.None) or in a break with BreakCasting off are also stood down without the driver taking over. Reword it so a host author reading it doesn't count on the fallback.

findings.title: RightClick runs every hook's Vote before checking the mouse is over the button
findings.detail: On every right-click MouseDown anywhere on screen (map orders included), each visible ability gizmo calls Offers, which runs HasWorker and every AbilityAIHooks vote, and only then checks Mouse.IsOver. Moving the Mouse.IsOver(rect) check (line 190) above the Offers call (line 189) makes this one rect test for every gizmo the cursor isn't over.

findings.title: Load restores modes through the static Instance rather than this component
findings.detail: PostLoadInit calls the static SetMode, which resolves Instance (instance.world == Find.World) or falls back to Find.World?.GetComponent. If that ever names another component or null, the loaded modes are dropped or written elsewhere without any message. Writing into this.modes directly in the PostLoadInit loop removes the dependency.

findings.title: Badge runs the veto hooks on every repaint for each gizmo with a mode set
findings.detail: Badge calls AbilityAIHooks.NotVetoed on each Repaint for every ability button whose pawn has a non-Off mode. That is correct for Entad's request, but its frame cost is whatever the hooks cost. Worth knowing if a hook is slow; no change needed now.
